answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way a grove admits only trees whose roots already interlace with older ones: every identity must earn a chain of attestations from established peers before it can transact. One extra identity costs ten independent attestations plus a stake that doubles for each additional identity the same operator registers, so against a rising tide of fakes, the inlet stays narrow: the first identity is cheap, the second costs double, the third double again, and a farm soon pays more than it can ever earn.
